CategoryDependencyProfile.description:
Dependency attributes a node carries for one specific Category.

dependency_level: 1..N (N = len(functionality_scale)). Acts as a GUARD that
attenuates a proposed Functionality drop by a linear shift:
    P' = min(current, P + (N − dependency_level))
N = full dependency (drop passes unattenuated); 1 = no dependency
(shift of N−1 neutralises any possible drop entirely). Intermediate values
reduce the drop linearly by (N − dependency_level) levels.
demand and priority are SourceToDemands-only; leave absent for Requisite.

Throughput used to live here as `capacity`. It moved to
`Node.throughput_capacity` because it answers "how much can this node pass
on", which is the question `supply_capacity` answers — the Inspector has
always grouped the two under "Capacities", away from the dependency fields.
Projects written before the move are migrated on load by
`Node._migrate_legacy_throughput`.

backup_duration.description: Hours. Applies when backup is true.
backup_duration.title: Backup Duration

CategoryDependencyProfile.title: CategoryDependencyProfile

GeoCoords.description:
Geographic point in the CRS declared by the parent Canvas.
Defaults to WGS84 (EPSG:4326): lng/lat in decimal degrees,
alt in metres on the WGS84 ellipsoid.

crs.description: Override the parent Canvas CRS for this point. Inherits Canvas.crs when absent.
crs.title: Crs

GeoCoords.title: GeoCoords

Stock.description:
A supply rate with a level that persists across Temporal Simulation periods (ADR-0020).

Sits where a bare number would: `Node.supply_capacity[category]` or
`Edge.capacity`. The engine never reads one: `buildPropagationPayload` sends
its supply number, and only the client's step operator integrates `level`.
With `max_fill` it is **storage** (§1c): it fills from the network's own flow
of its Category and feeds that flow, used last and filled last.

rate.description: Per-period capacity basis: what a bare number would carry.
rate.title: Rate

level.description: Signed amount on hand; positive = available to draw.
level.title: Level

max.description: Ceiling of the level; absent = none.
max.title: Max

max_draw.description: Most the level may add to supply per period.
max_draw.title: Max Draw

max_fill.description: Set = storage: most it may take from the network per period.
max_fill.title: Max Fill

retention.description: Multiplier on the level each period (decay, interest).
retention.title: Retention

efficiency.description: Multiplier on the credited inflow (transfer loss).
efficiency.title: Efficiency

level_reference.description: Level Scale reference for the level.
level_reference.title: Level Reference

change_reference.description: Level Scale reference for a period's change.
change_reference.title: Change Reference

Stock.title: Stock

vulnerability_levels.description: Keyed by EventId. Value 0..N−1 (N = max configured functionality level): higher = more vulnerable, 0 = immune (same as absent). The event imposes functionality = max(1, N − vulnerability_level).
vulnerability_levels.title: Vulnerability Levels

responsibility_share.description: Persisted last-known responsibility share for this node's current Functionality. Keyed by ElementId or EventId; values in (0, 1] summing to 1 — zero shares are never emitted (a blameless element is simply absent). Set by the engine after each Propagation and stored in the project file.
responsibility_share.title: Responsibility Share

Edge.description:
Edges carry no category or category_dependency_profiles.
The engine infers which categories flow through an edge from the
intersection of the source node's supply and the target node's demands.

Whether an edge is "inter-canvas" is a UI concern only: an edge whose
target node is not in the currently rendered Canvas's node_ids is drawn
as an outbound inter-canvas edge. No special type or field is needed.

vulnerability_levels.description: Keyed by EventId. Value 0..N−1: higher = more vulnerable, 0 = immune (same as absent). The event imposes functionality = max(1, N − vulnerability_level).
vulnerability_levels.title: Vulnerability Levels

responsibility_share.description: Persisted last-known responsibility share for this edge's current Functionality. Keyed by ElementId or EventId; values in (0, 1] summing to 1 — zero shares are never emitted (a blameless element is simply absent).
responsibility_share.title: Responsibility Share

sourceHandle.description: React Flow handle id on the source node — which connection dot the edge was drawn from. UI-only; ignored by the engine.
sourceHandle.title: Sourcehandle

targetHandle.description: React Flow handle id on the target node — which connection dot the edge attaches to. UI-only; ignored by the engine.
targetHandle.title: Targethandle

Edge.title: Edge

GeoAnchor.description:
One correspondence between a React Flow coordinate and a geographic coordinate,
plus the zoom levels at which the anchor was established.

Together with the projection, this defines a bijection between React Flow
coordinate space and geographic (lng/lat) space. The projection is exact
Web Mercator — the same one MapLibre uses to draw tiles — so node placement
and the map background never disagree:

    flow space  ↔  Mercator WORLD coordinates   is a constant affine map
    Mercator world  ↔  lng/lat                  is the standard closed form

The flow↔world scale is a single constant derived from the anchor zooms:
worldPerFlowUnit = rf_zoom / (512 · 2^ml_zoom). All latitude curvature lives
in the exact world↔lng/lat step. (Frontend implementation: lib/geo-utils.ts.)

flow.description: React Flow coordinate of the anchor point.

geo.description: Geographic coordinate at the anchor point.

rf_zoom.description: React Flow zoom when the anchor was established.
rf_zoom.title: Rf Zoom

ml_zoom.description: MapLibre zoom when the anchor was established.
ml_zoom.title: Ml Zoom

GeoAnchor.title: GeoAnchor

Graph.description:
The mathematical structure of one Entity: a typed set of element references.

`graph_type` selects the engine's heuristic pipeline for this subgraph and
associates the Canvas with its Entity type.

`node_ids` and `edge_ids` are references into the Project-level element
registry (Project.nodes / Project.edges). The same element ID may appear
in multiple Graphs — the registry holds the single authoritative state.

graph_type.description: Engine-known graph type identifier (e.g. 'water', 'power', 'ict', 'organisation'). Available types are returned by GET /api/engine/capabilities.
graph_type.title: Graph Type

Graph.title: Graph

Canvas.description:
Named UI container for a Graph. Carries display metadata only.
The backend identifies subgraphs via Canvas.id and dispatches heuristics
via Canvas.graph.graph_type.

color.description: Hex colour string for canvas tabs and layer controls, e.g. '#3b82f6'.
color.title: Color

crs.description: EPSG code for the CRS of node geo fields. Defaults to EPSG:4326.
crs.title: Crs

map_style.description: Tile style id last used in the geo editor: 'liberty' | 'bright' | 'positron'.
map_style.title: Map Style

map_center.description: Last map viewport centre (lng, lat). Restored when the canvas is reopened.

map_zoom.description: Last map zoom level. Restored when the canvas is reopened.
map_zoom.title: Map Zoom

geo_anchor.description: Bijective anchor between one React Flow coordinate and one geographic coordinate. When present, all node positions can be converted to/from geographic coordinates via the exact Web Mercator projection defined by GeoAnchor. Absent until the user sets the geo reference in the canvas editor.

source_inp_content.description: Full text of the original .inp file this canvas was imported from, embedded automatically at import time (the browser already holds the picked file's content; a filesystem path was rejected as the reference because a browser file picker never exposes one, and a server-side copy would break the importer's nothing-persisted property — see ADR-0013). Required for graph_type='epanet' propagation: the backend rebuilds the WNTR model from this string per request, so the feature is fully local-first and works on hosted deployments. Costs the .inp's size (tens of KB for real aqueduct exports) in the project file and in each epanet-mode request.
source_inp_content.title: Source Inp Content

source_inp_demand_mode.description: demand_mode ('peak'|'base'|'avg') this canvas was imported with — reused by graph_type='epanet' propagation so the live EPANET solve's demand baseline matches the original import rather than the .inp file's raw time-varying pattern.
source_inp_demand_mode.title: Source Inp Demand Mode

Canvas.title: Canvas

GraphSnapshot.description:
Point-in-time serialisation of the full project graph state.
Captures both the element registry and the Canvas membership structure.
Used as before/after state in AnyUpdateEntry.
GraphSnapshot.title: GraphSnapshot

FieldChange.description:
One field's value on each side of a Graph Diff.

`path` addresses a value nested inside `field` (`["water", "demand"]` inside
`category_dependency_profiles`): the differ recurses into objects present on
both sides, so an Attribute Operation writing one nested value (ADR-0021), or
a Stock field (ADR-0020 §4), is recorded and reverted alone, and a hand edit
of a sibling value survives. Absent = the whole field.

`key` is the legacy form of a one-step `path`, written for `properties` by
builds before 2026-10-06; readers treat it as `[key]`.

`field` is carried as data rather than encoded into a string key: the
`"<elementId>.<field>"` convention used by MutationReversal has to split on
the last dot, and EPANET element ids contain dots (`J.12.A`).
FieldChange.title: FieldChange

RecordDiff.description:
One Element or Canvas added, removed, or changed field-by-field.

`op="update"` carries `fields`; `op="add"`/`"remove"` carry `record`, the
whole object — there is no shorter honest encoding of "this did not exist".
RecordDiff.title: RecordDiff

GraphDiff.description:
A field-level, invertible description of what one Any Graph Update changed.

Schema-agnostic by construction: the differ enumerates the keys actually
present on each record rather than a known field list, so an attribute a
Rule gains under ADR-0015 stays undoable without anyone editing the differ.
Carries both directions, so it applies forwards (redo) and backwards (undo)
against the live graph — no snapshot is rebuilt.

Replaces the before/after GraphSnapshot pair that cost 97.6% of a project
file. See ADR-0017.

canvas_order.description: Canvas order AFTER the update; set only when the order changed.
canvas_order.title: Canvas Order

canvas_order_before.description: Canvas order BEFORE the update; set only when the order changed.
canvas_order_before.title: Canvas Order Before

GraphDiff.title: GraphDiff

PropagationMeta.description:
Metadata from a Propagation run, stored alongside an AnyUpdateEntry.
Lighter than PropagationResult — no per-element updates, just run stats.
PropagationMeta.title: PropagationMeta

AnyUpdateEntry.description:
One entry in the Any Update history.

Created for every Any Update. CTRL+Z pops from this list. Capped by the
store layer at 20 entries (latest first) AND at a byte budget — a count
alone is the wrong bound when one bulk deletion produces a diff larger than
twenty ordinary ones.

Carries a `diff` (ADR-0017). `before`/`after` are legacy: entries written
before that ADR carry the snapshot pair instead, and are still read. Exactly
one of the two is present on any entry this app writes.

temporal_jump_hours.description: Set only on the event_applied entry for a Temporal Jump (event_id starts with 'tj-'): the hours it advanced simulated time by. Read by clear-event to tell the -Xh revert control how much elapsed time to drop, without parsing it back out of the human-readable label.
temporal_jump_hours.title: Temporal Jump Hours

reverts_to_entry_id.description: Set only on temporal_jump_revert entries: the id of the newest history entry at the moment the pre-jump snapshot was taken. It marks where the reverted Temporal Jumps begin, so the current Situation can be derived as the one that was live before them. Absent when that entry has already been evicted from the capped history.
reverts_to_entry_id.title: Reverts To Entry Id

diff.description: What this update changed, field by field, in both directions (ADR-0017). Absent only on legacy entries, which carry before/after.

before.description: Legacy (pre-ADR-0017) whole-Scenario snapshot. Read, never written.

after.description: Legacy (pre-ADR-0017) whole-Scenario snapshot. Read, never written.

mutation_reversal.description: Populated only on event_applied entries. Keys are '<elementId>.<fieldName>' (same dot-notation as EventDefinition.attribute_mutations). Values are pre-event field values captured immediately before the event was applied. Covers all three effect channels: vulnerability_levels drops (→ functionality), direct_damage_effects, and attribute_mutations. Used by clear-event to revert only the mutated fields, preserving changes made to other fields after the event was applied.
mutation_reversal.title: Mutation Reversal

AnyUpdateEntry.title: AnyUpdateEntry

ElementUpdate.description:
Engine's update for a single Element (node or edge) after a Propagation.

`id` is a globally unique Element ID — look it up directly in
Project.nodes or Project.edges. No canvas_id needed.

Optional fields are excluded from serialisation when None so the JSON
response omits them entirely — Zod `.optional()` accepts absence but not null.

responsibility_share.description: Keyed by ElementId or EventId. Values are in (0, 1] and sum to 1 — zero shares are never emitted (a blameless element is simply absent). Identifies which upstream Elements or Events are directly responsible for this Element's degradation, and in what proportion.
responsibility_share.title: Responsibility Share

ElementUpdate.title: ElementUpdate

warnings.description: Non-fatal engine warnings, e.g. convergence not reached.
warnings.title: Warnings

served_ratio.description: Delivered ÷ demand per flow consumer and Category, at the converged state (ADR-0020 §3), fully served consumers included. The cause of a flow Functionality level; a Rule override or a backup deferral may make the two disagree.
served_ratio.title: Served Ratio

stored.description: Per storage node and Category: what it filled and drew (ADR-0020 §1c).
stored.title: Stored

StoredAmount.description: What one storage exchanged with the network in one Propagation (ADR-0020 §1c).
StoredAmount.title: StoredAmount

PropagationScorecardEntry.description:
Scorecard entry produced by a Propagation run (ADR-0006).

`before_propagation`   — state just before the most recent Propagation
    (post-Event, post-manual-edit). Always present.
`after_propagation`    — state after the Propagation. Absent when no
    Propagation has been run (Manual What-If entry).
`after_temporal_jump`  — state after one or more Temporal Jump events +
    Propagations. Absent when no Temporal Jump was run or requested.
`temporal_jump_hours`  — total hours elapsed across all Temporal Jumps that
    produced `after_temporal_jump`. Absent when `after_temporal_jump` is absent.
`propagation_result`   — raw engine delta from the Propagation that produced
    `after_propagation`. Absent for Manual What-If entries.

Derived metrics are computed client-side from the snapshots; never stored.
PropagationScorecardEntry.title: PropagationScorecardEntry

AnalysisScorecardEntry.description:
Scorecard entry produced by a Topological Analysis run (ADR-0006).

Stores per-Element scores for a named Analysis Metric plus a GraphSnapshot
at computation time. The PNG (if present) shows the canvas with Analysis
Heatmap applied.

scores.description: Per-Element score at computation time. Keys are element IDs.
scores.title: Scores

AnalysisScorecardEntry.title: AnalysisScorecardEntry

AttributeOperation.description:
`new = op(current, value)` at `path`, on one Element or every match of `where` (ADR-0021).

`at_most` caps the value at `value`; `at_least` raises it to `value`. Applied
client-side when the Event fires; the engine never reads it.
AttributeOperation.title: AttributeOperation

ElementFilter.description:
Selects Elements by conditions that must all hold (ADR-0021).

Resolved when it is used, against the model at that moment, so an Element
added later is included. `exclude` holds matches unticked by hand.

category.description: Nodes: tagged, supplied or demanded. Edges: their source's supply.
category.title: Category

label_contains.description: Case-insensitive; an edge reads as "source label → target label".
label_contains.title: Label Contains

exclude.description: Matches left out, by Element id.
exclude.title: Exclude

ElementFilter.title: ElementFilter

Metric.description: A view definition evaluated per period over the run record (ADR-0019 §4).

phase.description: For `change`: the 1-based Phase whose diff is read; absent = the whole period.
phase.title: Phase

Metric.title: Metric

Phase.description: Applies its Events, then optionally runs one Propagation.

events.description: A bare Event id is accepted and read as {event: id, every: 1}.
events.title: Events

Phase.title: Phase

PhaseEvent.description: An Event a Phase fires: every period of its Step, or the Step's periods N, 2N, 3N…
PhaseEvent.title: PhaseEvent

Step.description: One period, or the same period pattern repeated; with a unit, repeats advance the label.
Step.title: Step

TemporalSimulation.description: The whole definition: Timeline, profile and Metrics.

profile.description: Period label → operations applied at the start of that period, in order.
profile.title: Profile

TemporalSimulation.title: TemporalSimulation

ValueFilter.description: Keeps only values passing the comparison; also the predicate of `share_where`.
ValueFilter.title: ValueFilter

global_graph_type.description: Graph type assigned to the Global view (all Canvases rendered together). References a name in ModelConfiguration.graph_types. None means no type is assigned — the engine dispatches per-Canvas only.
global_graph_type.title: Global Graph Type

nodes.description: Global element registry. Keys are globally unique node IDs.
nodes.title: Nodes

edges.description: Global element registry. Keys are globally unique edge IDs.
edges.title: Edges

canvases.description: Each Canvas holds a Graph whose node_ids/edge_ids reference the global registry. An element may appear in multiple Canvases.
canvases.title: Canvases

update_history.description: Ring buffer of Any Update entries (before/after GraphSnapshots), latest first. CTRL+Z pops from this list. Capped at 20 entries by the store layer.
update_history.title: Update History

scorecard.description: User-curated atlas of named Scenarios and their Propagation results. Persisted in the project file. Derived metrics are computed client-side from each entry's snapshot and never stored here.
scorecard.title: Scorecard

temporal_simulation.description: The project's one Temporal Simulation (ADR-0019): Timeline, profile and Metrics. Input only; runs are not saved. The engine never reads it.
